resource_only_exploratory_contract.scope: Historical scalar-open resource-only contract; host-pressure thresholds are superseded by host_pressure_disposition for all M4 benchmark modes
resource_only_exploratory_contract.latency_diagnostic: Exactly seven scalar counts (0–6) x HNSW/FLAT x three repetitions; create/close/reopen/close; 84 API opens, empty roots, no documents or queries. Record each create-and-open and reopen API wall interval; exclude schema construction, close, shutdown, and cleanup. Evidence class EXPLORATORY / NON-QUALIFYING; API-level timing only, not internal stage attribution.
resource_only_exploratory_contract.workspace_capacity_unverified_label: WORKSPACE_CAPACITY_UNVERIFIED when workspace traversal or mutation coverage is incomplete; preserve UNKNOWN/INCOMPLETE without converting workload completion into capacity PASS or verified peak.
resource_only_exploratory_contract.load1: Load-1 is observation-only in every M4 mode: record baseline and runtime values and analyze them as host context; never use M4-RG-LOAD as an admission, abort, or inter-arm gate. Keep the historical threshold and raw PASS/FAIL observations unchanged.
resource_only_exploratory_contract.host_swap_reclaim: Record baseline-to-runtime pswpin, pswpout, direct scan/steal, and allocstall deltas; analyze direction and magnitude without attributing host-wide movement to M4. Positive deltas alone are not distress and do not block.
resource_only_exploratory_contract.hard_stop_signals: Host OOM kill increment, telemetry counter regression or missing required safety counters, approved swap-capacity or retained disk-reserve failure, cgroup cap/limit/OOM distress, timeout, workload correctness failure, required safety-telemetry loss, or cleanup/containment failure remain blocking. Host PSI, load and MemAvailable thresholds are never stop signals.
resource_only_exploratory_contract.reserve_policy: Retain actual per-operation cgroup memory/swap/task limits, runtime timeout, host OOM observation, and disk reserve. MemAvailable, PSI and load threshold comparisons are telemetry only; no 3 GiB MemAvailable floor is an admission/abort gate.
resource_only_exploratory_contract.workspace: Retain UNKNOWN/INCOMPLETE for races or lost coverage. Never claim verified peak storage from sampled traversal, and never report a soft-budget observation as PASS or hard-cap proof. Existing fatal scope/permission/I/O/overflow and safety-telemetry failures still block.
resource_only_exploratory_contract.no_retroactive_rewrite: A contract amendment changes interpretation only; raw receipts and historical execution records remain immutable, and no retry is implied.

contention_aware.launch_requires: For shared_collection_pair, use a fresh unique operation id/root and record the bounded budget. Host PSI, load and MemAvailable thresholds are telemetry only and never block launch. Actual cgroup resource caps/events, approved swap-capacity and retained-disk reserves, required safety telemetry, correctness, durability, timeout, and cleanup remain mandatory. One matched pair per operation; no automatic retry after a blocked/failed operation.
contention_aware.historical_envelope: All four raw comparisons remain unchanged and recorded as PASS/FAIL; in this explicitly selected mode only they are measurement context, not universal safety limits or launch/abort criteria
contention_aware.baseline_pressure: Record original first-three-window memory/swap bounds and drift for attribution; PSI is observational, and no idle/stationary host prerequisite applies. Enforce only actual swap/disk capacity, cgroup containment, telemetry integrity and correctness/durability checks
contention_aware.resource_controls: Required finite M4 cgroup CPU quota, memory.max, memory.swap.max and pids.max (tasks/threads); workspace allocated/apparent monitored soft budgets only in this exploratory mode. Retained-disk reserve, cgroup distress, timeout, correctness/durability and verified cleanup remain mandatory. No host MemAvailable/PSI/load threshold gate, filesystem quota, aggregate hard workspace cap or I/O isolation claim
contention_aware.capacity_basis: Agent-authored per-operation resource estimates with resource_basis, within cgroup limits and disk/swap safety controls; no MemAvailable-derived host reservation gate. Record MemAvailable/load/PSI as context, never as launch/abort criteria. SwapFree covers remaining approved M4 swap allocation; filesystem free space covers unconsumed workspace allocation plus disk reserve.
contention_aware.monitoring: Host PSI/load/MemAvailable, swap/diskstats, and owned process/cgroup CPU, memory, swap, task counts/limit events, PSI and process-tree I/O remain recorded. Host PSI/load/MemAvailable are observational. Known workspace publication races retain INCOMPLETE/UNKNOWN without abort; sampled soft-budget breaches warn with observed/limit/excess bytes. Unverifiable scope/permission/I/O errors, missing required safety telemetry, monitor gap, OOM/limit distress, swap/disk reserve failure, controller/cleanup failure or timeout stop the operation, never unrelated workloads
contention_aware.recovery: Three consecutive valid ten-second safety-capacity/integrity windows; no host-pressure threshold or stationary-baseline requirement. First-arm failure blocks arm two; recovery timeout/integrity/disk-or-swap capacity failure consumes the attempt without retry
contention_aware.isolation_scope: Operation-bound full-sync 500x20 A/A, the owner-authorized shared-collection 500x5 A/B follow-up pair defined below, or separately authorized bounded M4 exploratory diagnostics including multi-arm compaction-contention; qualification, legacy diagnostics, other benchmarks and production unchanged
contention_aware.no_attribution_shortcut: Host-wide pressure is not evidence that M4 caused it; observed during-minus-baseline is temporal association, not identified incremental causality

shared_collection_pair.measurement_semantics: Compare five writer-cycle samples and at least 320 concurrent hybrid-reader queries per arm descriptively. Four reader threads run continuously from writer-cycle start through commit plus GC completion, with at least 16 queries per reader per writer cycle; counts may exceed the 320-query minimum and must be reported per reader-cycle. Writer nearest-rank p95 at n=5 is the maximum, not a stable-tail estimate. Record initial/per-cycle native and M4 opens, M4 apply/flush, native upsert/flush, GC/compaction/checkpoint, per-query vector/FTS/merge and lock waits, process CPU/I/O, cgroup peaks/events, retained bytes, post-arm snapshot coherence, and host I/O PSI throughout. I/O PSI is host-wide observational context only for this benchmark, not an admission or abort gate; disclose elevated or mismatched host pressure as a measurement limitation. Do not claim causality, qualification, or a universal architecture win.

wal_replay_probe_policy.purpose: Measure identical WAL-only ApplyBatch writes and fresh Index::Open replay in both arms, with stats-event coalescing disabled to isolate LZ4 compression
wal_replay_probe_policy.durability: WAL fsync remains enabled for every bounded ApplyBatch; close without Flush, advise only this fresh probe index's regular files with POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED, verify residency with mincore, then replay and verify live-doc count plus searchable postings
metrics: target-index file bytes and mincore resident pages before/after cache advice
wal_replay_probe_policy.limitation: The probe attempts to evict only the fresh index's file pages; only zero mincore residency supports calling those target files cold. Kernel/library and all unrelated host caches remain warm, so this is not a fully cold-machine start.

immutable_write_amplification_pair.measurement_semantics: Counterbalanced delta512-to1536 comparisons repeatedly reduced process writes15.0% and segment writes36.83%, compactions6-to-2, but an order-specific query p95 outlier remains; do not change max_delta_docs default. A 4-vs16MiB stats-log threshold pair reduced process writes1.05% with unchanged WAL/segment counters and exact retrieval, but replay-open time regressed18.5%; reject16MiB and retain4MiB default. Reporter reopen-stage parity bug was fixed and covered. A 256-vs512 mutation-chunk attempt was blocked before initial indexing by the supported ApplyBatch cap; preserve256 and do not retry or bypass. Three cap4-vs5 pairs at delta1536 showed consistent segment-write reduction10.12%, process-write reductions2.36-4.06%, and compactions2-to-1 with exact correctness and complete workspace accounting. Median query p95 across pairs/orders stayed within10%; one control-first pair regressed11.1% initial and16.4% burst3. Retain cap5 only as a research candidate; no default change. The first stats-event coalescing pair (candidate first) preserved exact snapshot/oracle/retrieval/reopen parity. Candidate process writes were40,849,400 B vs45,211,600 B (-9.65%); segment writes and WAL bytes were unchanged. Final non-WAL bytes fell4,507,390 B and the candidate stats log was10,207 B vs0 B after the control checkpoint. Query p95 candidate was no slower by >10% at any stage, though burst2 was31% faster and one arm had shared-workspace accounting UNKNOWN; therefore exploratory only, performance-ineligible. Three pre-durability-fix pairs preserved exact snapshot/oracle/retrieval/reopen parity. Process writes fell8.48-9.65% per pair and9.20% pooled; WAL/segment bytes and fsync counts were unchanged. Candidate-first repeats had p95 within10% at all stages but incomplete workspace accounting; control-first was fully accounted but burst3 regressed10.6%. Retain coalescing as a research-only candidate; REWORK performance qualification and do not change defaults. Under the corrected strict file/directory sync, two counterbalanced coalescing pairs each reduced process writes8.7-10.7%, with exact snapshot/retrieval parity. Control-first had p95 regressions13-25%; candidate-first had30-92% and INCOMPLETE_WORKSPACE_CAVEAT, with external host load/process activity visible. The latency results are order/host-contended and not causal; no default change. An offline probe over actual M4 WAL frames (15.99MB,19 txns) found LZ4 default compresses to5.46MB (-65.9%) at34ms CPU; zstd1 to2.87MB (-82.0%) at58ms; zlib1 to3.12MB (-80.5%) at173ms. Select LZ4 for an opt-in, versioned, backward-replay-compatible prototype; preserve fsync boundaries and feature OFF by default. Five P4 WAL-LZ4 pairs preserved exact logical/retrieval/reopen parity; four were workspace-complete and one had INCOMPLETE_WORKSPACE_CAVEAT. WAL appended bytes fell19.758MB→6.752MB (-65.83%), segment bytes/fsync counts unchanged; process-attributed writes fell22.16-27.93% per pair and25.05% pooled. Query p95 reversed with order both before and after untimed query warmup: warm candidate-first was10.5-41.8% faster, warm control-first was10.6-21.4% slower on bursts. No causal latency conclusion; retain LZ4 OFF and evidence non-qualifying. A candidate-first warm-query stats-coalescing pair preserved exact snapshots/reopen, logical oracle, PK sets, ranking and scores (0 mismatch; top-10 Jaccard1.000). Candidate process writes were53.16MB vs control57.98MB (-8.31%); WAL appends, segment writes, fsync counts and compactions were identical. Candidate warmed-query p95 was within+3.4%/-23.3% of control across stages; delete-batch latency varied strongly by arm position. The second arm's workspace sampling was UNKNOWN, so the pair is exploratory and performance-ineligible despite no budget warnings. The control-first warm-query counterbalance is complete. Two counterbalanced LZ4 OFF/ON target-index-file-cold replay roots preserved zero resident target pages and recovery, but replay-open, ACK and write-CPU effects reversed with order; both roots are workspace-incomplete/non-qualifying. Keep LZ4 opt-in/OFF by default; fully cold-machine start remains unmeasured. Host PSI/load/MemAvailable remain telemetry only; no safety controls are relaxed. Preserve artifacts; never retry after an actual safety refusal/stop. The 2026-10-24 coalescing+LZ4 combined P4 control-first and candidate-first pairs both preserved exact snapshots, oracle, ranking and retrieval (0 mismatch; Jaccard 1.000) and each reduced process-attributed writes about39.0% and WAL appends65.8%; both remain performance-ineligible because known inotify/workspace traversal races yielded UNKNOWN sampled peaks. Candidate-first query p95 stayed within+9.8%, but delete-batch p95 varied by order. In the same candidate-first root, an isolated coalescing-OFF LZ4-only ApplyBatch probe reduced WAL 16.073MB→5.485MB (65.87%) and probe physical writes17.412MB→6.251MB (64.1%); durable ApplyBatch ACK p95 62.5ms vs68.4ms and warm fresh-index replay-open 1.046s vs1.042s were similar. This is one pair, same-process page cache, not cold media; do not infer qualification. Candidate ACK p95 was lower in both roots, but the candidate/control gap differed sharply by order; both workspace-incomplete probes remain non-qualifying and establish no stable latency effect. M4 correctness tests cover mixed legacy/LZ4 frames, checksum corruption, torn suffix, post-fsync crash recovery/searchability, coalescing replay and flush crash boundaries; no default change. The counterbalanced LZ4-ON/coalescing-OFF-vs-ON interaction pair completed with COMPLETE workspace receipts and exact parity; process writes fell9.97% and13.62% (11.80% pooled), stats-log bytes3.526MB→10,207B, with WAL/segment/fsync/compaction counters equal. Keep coalescing opt-in; no default change, and the pair remains exploratory/non-qualifying. Host PSI/load/MemAvailable are telemetry only; actual disk/cgroup/runtime/watchdog/required telemetry/correctness/durability/cleanup remain enforced. Standing authorization applies; one pair per fresh root; no retry after a blocked/failed operation.

memory_probe.measurement_semantics: Independent memory-scaling diagnostic: seed 4,096 documents instead of 8,192, retaining the same four arms, four writers, 32 logical writes, 64 reader queries, and all unchanged cgroup/disk/swap safety limits. This smaller fixture is explicitly non-comparable to the 8,192-document contract and all prior measurements; analyze memory growth and tracked compaction scratch only, not latency, causal effects, or architecture performance. One fresh operation only; actual capacity, containment, required telemetry, correctness, durability, and cleanup safety checks remain mandatory. Host-pressure thresholds are telemetry only. No retry after a safety failure.

memory_trace.measurement_semantics: One bounded phase-attribution operation: 1,024 seeds per arm (one seed/flush block), all four existing arms and their reopen verification, with the same 32 logical writes, 64 reader queries, dictionary, binary, cgroup/host reserves, and hard gates. This is a distinct, lower-volume diagnostic, not a retry of the 4,096-document memory_probe. Correlate CLOCK_BOOTTIME M4_PHASE markers with process PSS and cgroup samples to distinguish analyzer Open/reopen, seed/flush, concurrent compaction/writer/reader and post-flush phases. Do not claim performance comparison, lifetime-peak proof, or cause beyond correlated phases. One operation only; any gate abort is consumed and not retried.

memory_trace_after_snapshot_fix.measurement_semantics: One fresh, one-shot verification of the content-addressed native dictionary snapshot correction after source-level root-cause analysis and focused regression tests. The four-arm workload remains 1,024 seeds/arm with all original hard limits unchanged; the rebuilt binary has a new identity. This is not an automatic retry of the consumed pre-fix OOM operation. Correlate phase markers, process PSS and cgroup samples; retain the original OOM evidence. Any gate abort consumes this verification and is not retried. No latency/architecture comparison or performance claim.

memory_trace_scale2_after_snapshot_fix.measurement_semantics: One distinct 2,048-seed-per-arm post-fix memory-scaling operation under the unchanged existing hard/soft limits. It is not a retry of either consumed 4,096-document OOM or prior 1,024-document post-fix trace. Compare phase-correlated memory/cgroup data only; do not claim latency improvement or extrapolate capacity. Single operation; any preflight gate abort or runtime limit abort consumes this profile and is not retried.

memory_churn_two_versions.measurement_semantics: One distinct contained operation: run the existing 1,024-seed/four-arm workload under unchanged hard/soft caps, then initialize two sequential uncached Jieba analyzers from distinct content-addressed dictionary snapshots in the same process. Capture process smaps_rollup before, while live, and after each analyzer release; outer cgroup/PSS cadence captures transient peaks. This observes process residency across version-keyed analyzer initialization and release, alongside outer cgroup/PSS transient sampling; source tracing is needed to attribute retained bytes, and this is not allocator-stack attribution. This is a single exploratory probe, not a latency comparison or capacity claim. Any preflight/runtime abort consumes the profile and is not retried; do not increase caps.

memory_churn_two_versions_eviction.measurement_semantics: One distinct contained profile using the research-only cppjieba DictTrie cache-eviction overlay at the exact repository-relative binary path. First run the same 1,024-seed/four-arm workload under unchanged hard/soft caps, then initialize two distinct dictionary versions in one process and record per-version PSS/RSS before and after release. Compare retained/live-entry evidence against the prior uncapped one-entry cache implementation and same-workload baseline descriptively; this is not an isolated benchmark, causal attribution, latency comparison, or capacity claim. The source-level regression separately checks same-key coalescing, concurrent analyzer lifecycle, generation release, and reopening an older version. One fresh operation only; any preflight/runtime/containment failure consumes it and is not retried.

memory_churn_two_versions_trie_stream.measurement_semantics: One distinct same-cap exploratory cache-churn trace after the copy-reduction candidate. It removes per-analyzer temporary vector<Unicode> and pointer arrays by inserting the immutable base/user DictUnit entries directly into a local exception-safe Trie, in the same order; the existing public two-vector Trie constructor remains unchanged. Compare descriptively to the exact memory_churn_two_versions_memory_opt workload; record cgroup memory.stat, memory.peak, init times, and PSS, but this remains a one-run, multi-change research comparison, not isolated causal proof, stable latency/memory result, capacity claim, or architecture qualification. Any preflight/runtime/containment failure consumes the profile and is not retried.

memory_churn_two_versions_inline_child.measurement_semantics: One distinct same-cap cache-churn profile after direct trie streaming. It stores the first child edge inline in every TrieNode and allocates the unordered map only for additional children, reducing per-node map/bucket/hash-node overhead for the pinned base dictionary's frequent unary nodes. It also makes DeleteUserWord remove/prune the requested term rather than the pre-existing first-rune subtree. The legacy vector-taking Trie constructor remains and both entry paths are tested. Capture cgroup memory.stat, memory.peak, analyzer init times and PSS; compare descriptively with memory_churn_two_versions_trie_stream. Single-run multi-change exploratory evidence only, not causal proof, stable latency/memory, capacity or architecture qualification. Any preflight/runtime/containment failure consumes the profile and is not retried.

memory_churn_two_versions_concurrent_ope.measurement_semantics: Distinct same-cap diagnostic after the inline-child candidate. Two analyzers with different dictionary content fingerprints open concurrently, synchronize while both remain live for PSS sampling, then release one at a time. The inline-child overlay uses a bounded native cache (one retained path entry plus weak slots while older generations remain live); this measures co-resident analyzers and concurrent initialization, not an unbounded native-cache map. Compare only descriptively with the sequential two-version profile. Capture cgroup memory.stat/peak, phase markers, process PSS, and release observations. Exploratory memory/lifecycle evidence only, not a latency claim, stable capacity result, or architecture qualification. Any preflight/runtime/containment failure consumes the profile and is not retried.

memory_churn_two_versions_concurrent_all.measurement_semantics: Distinct follow-up to memory_churn_two_versions_concurrent_open with mallinfo2 allocator snapshots added to the same process-memory records. Reports current allocated heap+mmapped bytes and free arena bytes at baseline, concurrent-live, and each release point to help distinguish allocator-owned live memory from RSS/PSS residency. No profile caps or workload change; exploratory ownership accounting only, not a latency or capacity result. One operation, no retry if any gate or containment issue occurs.

memory_churn_two_versions_memory_opt.measurement_semantics: One exploratory same-workload/same-cap comparison with memory_churn_two_versions_eviction. The source-only research patch replaces a full DictUnit sort-copy with scalar weight min/max/median selection and moves parsed DictUnit storage into the immutable cache entry. Lifecycle and exact min/median/max user-weight tests pass. Capture cgroup memory.stat and per-version PSS/init timing; this single run is directional, not an isolated causal measurement, stable performance result, or capacity claim. Any preflight/runtime/containment failure consumes the profile and is not retried.

writer_group_commit.measurement_semantics: A single bounded, two-arm exploratory test of the opt-in M4 Upsert group-commit prototype versus ordinary per-call Upsert. Both arms use identical 1,024-document seeds, four concurrent writers × eight independent Upsert calls, two concurrent search readers, one default compaction, explicit flush, reopen verification, WAL fsync enabled, and unchanged containment/resource caps. Group commit coalesces only overlapping calls for at most 500 us or four records, persists them using existing atomic ApplyBatch WAL/replay semantics, then publishes the group atomically; this remains linearizable for overlapping calls but may add bounded queue delay. Record end-to-end per-call latency, pre-dispatch group-formation wait, per-call batch-size evidence (require at least one multi-record group), reader latency, WAL fsync counts, and durability/reopen checks; do not compare against the older ApplyBatch API arm as identical call semantics. One operation only; any preflight/runtime/containment failure consumes it and is not retried. Exploratory evidence, not qualification or production authorization.

writer_group_commit_per_upsert.measurement_semantics: A separately consumed, bounded two-arm test comparing ordinary per-call durable Upsert against per-Upsert WAL records sharing only the fsync for overlapping calls. Both arms use identical 1,024-document seeds, four concurrent writers × eight individual Upsert calls, two concurrent search readers, default compaction, explicit flush, reopen verification, WAL fsync enabled, and unchanged containment/resource caps. The candidate appends one independently replayable WAL frame per Upsert, fsyncs the complete frame prefix once, then applies individual records with a reader-visible boundary per Upsert; this intentionally does not provide ApplyBatch atomicity. Verify multiple records per shared fsync, per-call ACKs only after durable sync and apply, WAL sequence order, reader-visible prefixes, crash recovery before/after sync and between applies, and no post-fsync mutation after an uncertain sync/apply error. Capture per-call writer latency, queue wait/group size, fsync count, reader latency, and durability/reopen checks. One fresh operation only; any preflight/runtime/containment failure consumes it and is not retried. Exploratory evidence only; no production authorization.

writer_group_commit_snapshot_rebase.measurement_semantics: One distinct, bounded paired experiment testing whether the opt-in ordered Upsert group-commit queue adds value when both arms use the existing WAL-preserving snapshot-rebase compaction. The direct and group-commit arms use identical 1,024-document seeds, four writers × eight individual Upsert calls, two search readers, one concurrent snapshot-rebase compaction, explicit flush, reopen verification and WAL fsync; resource and containment caps are unchanged. The paired direct arm distinguishes the queue effect within this operation; compare it descriptively with the separately consumed default-compaction profile only, not as a controlled four-way comparison. Capture per-call writer latency, group wait/size, state-lock and compaction stages, reader samples, fsync counts, and durability/reopen checks. One fresh operation only; any preflight/runtime/containment failure consumes it and is not retried. No qualification, stable-tail claim, architecture win, or production authorization.

flush_reader_staging_pair.measurement_semantics: One bounded paired same-binary comparison of the pre-staging flush query-lock boundary (baseline) versus metadata publication staging (candidate). Each arm seeds the same 8,192 Jieba documents, runs four WAL-durable writers × eight Upserts with two readers during one default compaction, then starts two continuous readers before explicit Flush and keeps them active until at least two post-flush queries each. The verifier requires per-reader timestamps proving at least two completed queries before, one query started during and overlapping the flush interval, and two queries after; a larger query count without interval overlap is invalid. Both modes preserve WAL fsync, manifest-before-publication and reopen/replay semantics. Capture per-query total wall, native query-mutex wait and execution CPU; flush total/stage wall+CPU and query-lock wait/hold; writer p95/state wait; fsync and bytes-written counters; cgroup/host memory, CPU and I/O evidence. Single operation only, no retry if any gate, containment or overlap check fails. Exploratory evidence, not qualification, a stable p95 claim, or production authorization. Concurrent flush remains out of scope.

writer_group_commit_flush_reader_pair.measurement_semantics: Distinct, one-shot paired experiment following the direct flush-staging pair: compare ordinary Upsert against bounded four-record/500-us Upsert group commit while both arms use metadata staging, the same 8,192-document corpus, default compaction, two readers, 32 logical writes, WAL fsync, explicit flush and reopen/replay checks. During each arm, retain the established concurrent-reader/compaction phase and then run continuous timestamped readers across explicit Flush; require at least two completed queries per reader before and after plus a query starting and overlapping the native flush interval, corroborated by M4_PHASE events. Capture writer wall/state wait and group size/queue delay/fsyncs, reader total wall/native mutex wait/execution CPU for concurrent compaction and explicit flush, flush stage/query-lock/state-lock timings, bytes, cgroup/host resource and I/O evidence. Both arms keep atomic visibility and durability unchanged; group commit remains default-off. This is a new cross-factor comparison, not a retry of the consumed direct-vs-staging profile. Any gate, containment or overlap failure consumes this profile without retry. Exploratory only; not qualification, stable-tail claim, architecture win, or production authorization.

writer_group_commit_pending_flush_reader.measurement_semantics: A distinct one-shot follow-up to the consumed writer_group_commit_flush_reader_pair. That operation showed the default arm's post-writer explicit Flush had no pending delta and did not exercise metadata staging; do not infer reader-through-flush impact from its default-arm trace. This profile compares ordinary Upsert with bounded four-record/500-us Upsert group commit while both use metadata staging, with 8,192 seed documents and 32 concurrent logical writes. Immediately before the continuous-reader phase, each arm applies a separate 256-document WAL-durable batch with unique flushmarker terms; this intentionally leaves a bounded pending delta below max_delta_docs so the explicit Flush must persist real data. Verify exactly 256 flushmarker hits after close/reopen. Timestamp two continuously active readers across that flush; require at least two completed queries before/after, a started+overlapping query during it, phase-log corroboration, pending_flush_ms and nonzero segment build/write work. Preserve atomic publication and WAL durability. Capture writer/group queue and fsync metrics, reader wall/mutex/CPU, flush stages/locks, bytes, cgroup/host resource and I/O evidence. New profile, not retry or reuse of the prior one; any gate/containment/overlap/flush-work check failure consumes it without retry. Exploratory only; no stable-tail, architecture, qualification or production claim.

lock_contention_microbench.measurement_semantics: Within each arm, seed 8,192 Jieba-tokenized documents, run one compaction concurrently with four writers and two search readers (32 queries each), then Flush and verify after reopen. The default, snapshot, and snapshot_rebase arms use four WAL-durable writers making eight individual Upsert calls each. The apply_batch arm uses the same four writers and 32 logical mutations, but each writer submits eight mutations in one atomic, WAL-durable ApplyBatch call. This compares explicit client batching, not an internal autonomous group-commit queue. Writer timing is per API call: 32 Upsert samples versus four ApplyBatch samples; call p95 values have different units and sample counts and are not equivalent tail measures. The ApplyBatch arm uses default compaction. Compare the three compaction strategies plus the batch API arm in alternating root-hash order. With WAL enabled, rebase mode does not flush pending writer deltas at publication: it scans the uncommitted WAL for concurrent deletes, preserves their run dead-count/tombstone accounting, publishes only through the prior durable WAL sequence, and leaves the concurrent delta WAL-backed for normal later flush/replay. With WAL disabled, the existing pending-flush fallback remains. Rebase replaces only the captured immutable input runs; this is a research-only prototype and does not change the default API path. Record per-call writer wall times plus opt-in stage wall/CPU timings for normalization, state-mutex wait and hold, WAL encoding/append, query-mutex wait, apply and auto-flush; record query wall times and timing-schema-v5 diagnostics for compaction lock/pending-flush stages plus standalone post-writer Flush total, state/query lock wait/hold, and stage timings. Nested flush-stage schema v2 includes query-lock hold as an inclusive interval bounded by pending-flush duration and excluded from component-stage sums. Schema v5 extends the v4 writer API/call/logical-mutation binding; timing schemas 2–4 and nested flush-stage v1 historical receipts remain accepted. State-mutex wait is exact API lock acquisition time; hold timing accumulates only intervals with the state mutex owned and pauses across the unlocked snapshot merge build. merge_build includes streaming merge, reopen, and test-hook time. Residual wall time is not labeled scheduler time because it also includes other work. This 32-logical-write/64-query, one-round-per-arm operation is diagnostic only: no stable-tail claim, no cause attribution beyond instrumented stages, no qualification or architecture winner. Any superseded snapshot compaction is reported as such rather than hidden or retried.

workspace_observer.cost_semantics: Bounded streaming descriptor walk; cooperative deadline cannot bound a single blocked kernel filesystem syscall. No retry/rescan.
workspace_observer.snapshot_semantics: Complete traversal is a sampled observation, not an atomic snapshot, capacity upper bound or verified lifetime peak
workspace_observer.known_race: Retain ENOENT/directory mutation as partial observation, never COMPLETE/PASS. Legacy/qualification fail closed without proof; explicitly bound contention-aware exploratory mode may continue UNKNOWN under the owner-approved soft-budget contract.

contention_aware.pending_event_semantics: A readable queue after one drain is accounting UNKNOWN, not observed overflow. Only this exact issue plus known mutations may continue with raw UNVERIFIABLE/INCOMPLETE retained, valid root identity and all issue examples present. Actual overflow/unmount/truncated events, scope, permissions and I/O errors remain fatal. No extra drain/rescan.
contention_aware.breach_action: warn with raw observed/limit/excess bytes; never claim hard-cap enforcement
contention_aware.scope_error_action: abort; unknown scope, permission/EIO, actual overflow/unmount/truncated records and watch/scan work-budget failures are not accepted publication races. Pending readable queue alone is handled by the exact accounting-uncertainty rule, not fabricated complete telemetry
contention_aware.completion_semantics: Workspace uncertainty remains INCOMPLETE/UNKNOWN; completion with warnings is not PASS or qualifying evidence. All independent hard safety telemetry remains mandatory.

workspace_observer.reservation_credit: Zero: sampled gross allocated bytes are not a conservative lower bound on scoped physical allocation and cannot reduce shared-disk reserve requirements
workspace_observer.independent_capacity_proof: Unavailable by default; only the separately registered lock-contention microbenchmark may use its root-owned, policy-bound Btrfs simple-quota attestation. No external JSON, environment or fixture assertion can certify a bound

baseline_pressure_guard.evidence_class: baseline-derived host context from the first three valid 10-second windows; not a host admission limit
baseline_pressure_guard.enforcement: memory PSI is observation-only; an independently configured SwapFree capacity floor remains enforced, and telemetry-integrity failures remain blocking
baseline_pressure_guard.failure_scope: PSI contributes measurement context only, including when unavailable; only swap-capacity or required safety/workload telemetry-integrity failures affect the operation
baseline_pressure_guard.recovery: no recovery for PSI excursions; preserve snapshots; swap capacity must meet its explicit floor; no automatic retry

telemetry_integrity.enforcement: blocks measurement and qualification; never bypassed in diagnostic mode
telemetry_integrity.requirements: complete finite required safety/workload telemetry and valid monotonic sample brackets/cadence; host MemAvailable, load and PSI are optional context and may be missing/invalid without blocking launch, abort, stability classification or recovery

stability_envelope.enforcement: stability/host-pressure observations affect evidence classification and analysis only; they never block launch. Telemetry integrity, correctness, durability and actual containment checks remain enforced
stability_envelope.failure_scope: qualification validity or diagnostic evidence class only; never changes resource thresholds

interarm_recovery.enforcement: both modes require valid consecutive recovery windows, required safety/workload telemetry, retained-disk reserve, and any explicit swap-capacity floor before launching arm two; missing/invalid PSI/load/MemAvailable remain observational and do not block recovery
interarm_recovery.failure_scope: second arm only; preserve first-arm receipt and stop the pair if recovery does not pass

containment.mechanism: transient per-arm systemd user service and delegated cgroup v2 with independent watchdog
containment.io_limit_claim: Do not claim per-arm I/O throttling or physical-write attribution; record process-tree /proc I/O and host-wide diskstats as distinct scopes
containment.resource_budgets: No numeric cgroup memory, swap, CPU, or workspace ceilings are enabled unless separately approved; sampled workspace size is not a kernel quota
containment.test_fixture_override: The run_arm host-guard override is restricted to explicit M4_TEST_FIXTURE_MODE=1 synthetic commands in a temp-tree resource root; receipts label test_fixture_mode=true and performance_eligible=false. It is not exposed as a benchmark CLI option and must never wrap an M4 benchmark executable.
containment.cleanup: timeout/controller failure must terminate only the owned cgroup descendants, durably record the abort, and verify cleanup; never signal unrelated host processes

correctness_and_durability.authority: M4 invariants in research/m4-native/AGENTS.md, research/m4-native/README.md, oracle/regression tests, and approved format contracts
correctness_and_durability.enforcement: oracle/fault/recovery/sanitizer/build gates; a performance diagnostic cannot waive or downgrade a correctness/durability failure
correctness_and_durability.failure_scope: candidate/operation remains NO-GO; only an independently approved branch may continue

authority_precedence: current explicit user mission, authorization, and DoD
approved owner decisions and current repository policy
canonical handoff as state/evidence/continuity, not authority over newer user instructions

continuation_rules.operation_guard_failure: stop the affected benchmark/arm; do not bypass, weaken, auto-retry, or mark the whole mission done; continue only already-authorized independent safe work
continuation_rules.measurement_quality_failure: qualification evidence is invalid; only explicitly allowed exploratory diagnostics may continue after all resource, integrity, containment, and baseline-pressure guards pass
continuation_rules.correctness_or_durability_failure: block the candidate/operation and unsafe dependents; do not downgrade the gate or switch to an unapproved branch
continuation_rules.owner_decision_required: stop only the decision-dependent action; preserve the current state and continue unrelated safe authorized work
continuation_rules.mission_completion: requires reconciliation of every active mission DoD item; one operation, test, report, or no-launch is not mission success
continuation_rules.stale_handoff: reconcile a handoff next action against current user authorization and active mission scope before execution
continuation_rules.long_running_work: keep jobs interruptible and record job id, outputs, stop condition, and exact next action
continuation_rules.delegation: a sub-agent inherits the same scope and authority limits and cannot approve a gate change or mission completion

runner_mission_semantics: A benchmark runner may report only the operation and evidence class. It must never bypass a current gate or infer whole-mission SUCCESS from no-launch, one completed benchmark, one test, or one report. Whole-mission status belongs to the active mission DoD/handoff review.
